trips.title: Pelicans, Beech and Bujtina: Eastern Albania Off the Grid
trips.summary: Eastern Albania is the country's quiet half: a high plateau of lakes at 700-900 m, walled in by 2,200 m ridges, with the Greek and Macedonian borders on three sides and almost no coach tourism. This week starts in Korçë among Ottoman bazaar streets and the painted churches of Voskopojë, drops to the Prespa lakes where a Macedonian-speaking minority farms beans on the shore of a lake full of Dalmatian pelicans, then works north through Lin and Pogradec on Lake Ohrid before finishing in the beech forest of Shebenik-Jabllanicë, a UNESCO primeval-beech site and the best-documented Albanian habitat of the Balkan lynx. You sleep almost entirely in *bujtina*, family homestays where dinner is not optional and the rakia is homemade. It suits people who want genuinely empty landscape, are relaxed about rough road, and accept that most of the week is cash, no signal, and a wood stove.

trips.title: A Self-Catering Week in the Gesäuse Gorge
trips.sub: Gesäuse National Park, Ennstal Alps, Styria
trips.summary: Seven off-grid nights in a self-catering Almhütte above the Enns gorge, splitting wood, hauling water and watching chamois on the Xeis crags.

trips.title: Heathland Week, Cabin Days in the Hoge Kempen
trips.sub: Hoge Kempen National Park, Belgian Limburg
trips.summary: A gentle week of forest-cabin nights around Belgium's only national park, from heather-clad dunes to a former coal mine turned nature gate.

trips.title: The Una's Green Water: Cabins, Travertine and Krajina Forest
trips.summary: The Una is a limestone river that builds its own bed: dissolved calcium precipitates out as travertine, forming stepped barriers, terraces and curtains that shift over decades, so the waterfalls here are alive rather than eroded. Una National Park, declared in 2008, protects 198 km² of that river plus the Unac tributary and the forest above. This week is deliberately low-mileage, a rafting day from Štrbački buk, a slow day of village bread and travertine at Martin Brod, a forest day toward Klekovača's old-growth beech and spruce, and evenings on a wooden deck with the water going past at walking pace. It suits people who want genuine quiet, low prices and a country that still surprises Western visitors, and who will take the landmine briefing seriously enough to stay on marked ground.

trips.title: Reserve Country: Central Balkan Huts, Karst Caves and the Rhodope Vulture Gorges
trips.sub: Central Balkan National Park (Stara Planina), the Lovech karst, and the Eastern Rhodopes
trips.summary: A week in the two wildest blocks of Bulgaria: a beech-and-granite national park where nine strict reserves are sealed off from everything but a marked footpath, and a semi-desert river gorge where griffon vultures…

trips.title: Velebit Stone and Lika Forest: A Karst Cabin Week
trips.summary: Velebit is 145 km of waterless limestone standing between the Adriatic and the forested plateau of Lika, and this week works both sides of it. You start soft in the Gacka valley among watermills and trout springs, climb to Zavižan where Croatia's highest year-round weather station sits beside an alpine botanical garden, then walk the Premužić Trail, a 1930s dry-stone path engineered so beautifully that it crosses cliffs without a single exposed step. The middle of the week is deliberately slow: a day in the old-growth spruce of Štirovača, an afternoon at Kuterevo's bear refuge, a cave day underground. It ends on the seaward face at Paklenica, where the mountain drops 1,700 m to the sea in eight kilometres. It suits people who want silence, a wood stove, and no phone signal, and who accept that on this mountain you carry your own water.

trips.title: Bog and Wildwood, A Week in the Šumava Core
trips.summary: A week based at Modrava, walking boardwalked peat bogs and the Boubín primeval forest in Central Europe's largest continuous woodland, under strict national-park zoning.

trips.title: Praděd Country, A Chata Week in the Jeseníky
trips.sub: Jeseníky (Hrubý Jeseník), Moravian-Silesian and Olomouc Regions
trips.summary: A week of chata-to-chata days under Praděd, walking a glacial cirque of relict flora and a raised bog boardwalk in Moravia's highest range.

trips.title: Suðuroy & Mykines: Faroese Isolation Week
trips.summary: A seven-day nature escapes & cabin stay itinerary in Suðuroy (southernmost island) and Mykines (westernmost island), Faroe Islands.

trips.title: Saimaa Lakeland: Linnansaari & Kolovesi Cabin Week
trips.sub: Lake Saimaa, South Savo, Linnansaari and Kolovesi National Parks
trips.summary: A seven-day nature escapes & cabin stay itinerary in Lake Saimaa, South Savo, Linnansaari and Kolovesi National Parks, Finland.

trips.title: Hautes-Chaumes, A Marcairie Week on the Vosges Crest
trips.sub: Parc naturel régional des Ballons des Vosges, Haut-Rhin
trips.summary: A week of nights in working marcairies and fermes-auberges on the Vosges high pastures, walking the Route des Crêtes from the Grand Ballon to Lac Blanc.

trips.title: Let It Be Wild: A Week in the Bayerischer Wald
trips.summary: A week on Lusen and Rachel in Germany's oldest national park, with one off-grid night at Waldschmidthaus among the standing dead spruce the park deliberately left alone.

trips.title: Puszta, Karst and Szer: A Week in Hungary's Three Quietest National Parks
trips.summary: Three landscapes that share nothing except emptiness: the scattered ridge-hamlets of the Őrség, where a farmstead is its own village; the Hortobágy, Europe's largest continuous natural grassland, where in late…

trips.title: Limestone, Juniper and Pinnetta Smoke: A Supramonte Week
trips.summary: The Supramonte is the largest roadless limestone massif in Italy, a plateau of holm oak, juniper and dolines above the Gulf of Orosei, where shepherds lived in conical stone huts until living memory and where the interior still has no water on the surface for kilometres. This week works its three faces. You start inland at Oliena beside Su Gologone, Sardinia's biggest karst spring, walk up to the nuraghic village of Tiscali hidden inside a collapsed doline, then descend into Gorropu, a gorge 400 m deep and in places four metres wide. The middle of the week slows down for Orgosolo's murals and the granite of the Gennargentu. Then you cross to the Golgo plateau above Baunei, reached by a hairpin ramp and a dirt track, for the 270 m abyss of Su Sterru and the walk down to Cala Goloritzé, which now takes 250 people a day and no more. It finishes on the far coast at Bosa under griffon vultures. It suits people who want heat, silence, hard rock and dinner cooked by the family that raised it.

trips.title: Gauja & Slītere: Latvian Forest Cabin Week
trips.sub: Gauja National Park (Vidzeme) and Slītere National Park / Livonian Coast (northern Kurzeme)
trips.summary: A seven-day nature escapes & cabin stay itinerary in Gauja National Park (Vidzeme) and Slītere National Park / Livonian Coast (northern Kurzeme), Latvia.

trips.title: Lakeshore and Forest: A Week in the Upper Sûre
trips.summary: A quiet week around Luxembourg's drinking-water reservoir and its Öslinger forest, from a stone-tower town to a lakeside Naturpark chalet, using the country's free trains and buses to stay car-free.

trips.title: Limestone, Floodplain and Well Water: Seven Quiet Days in Rural Moldova
trips.sub: The Răut Canyon, the Dniester Cliffs & the Prut Floodplain
trips.summary: This is not wilderness and it does not pretend to be. It is a farmed country with three wild seams: a white limestone canyon where monks cut cells into the cliff, the wooded bluffs above the Dniester, and a Prut…

trips.title: Wet Heath and Dark Sky: A Week in Drenthe
trips.summary: A quiet week on the Netherlands' largest wet heathland, sleeping in a Drenthe cabin, walking to Stone Age tombs and a historic radio telescope under some of the darkest skies in the country.

trips.title: White Bicycles: A Week on the Veluwe
trips.summary: A week of free white bicycles, wildlife hides and the Kröller-Müller's van Goghs inside a fenced, ticketed national park, based in a forest cabin near Otterlo on the wider Veluwe.

trips.title: Katun Smoke and Lynx Country: A Šar-Mavrovo-Galičica Cabin Week
trips.summary: North Macedonia keeps its wildest ground in a north-south chain of limestone and old forest that almost nobody outside the Balkans walks: Šar Planina, made a national park only in 2021, then Mavrovo's 73,000 hectares of beech and spruce around an artificial lake with a drowned church in it, then Galičica riding the ridge between Ohrid and Prespa. This week moves down that chain slowly. You sleep in a shepherd's katun on the Bistra plateau, in a stone house in Galičnik where two people live year-round, and finally on the Ohrid shore. The centrepiece is Korab at 2,764 m, the country's high point, sitting exactly on the Albanian border, reached through a military-controlled zone. Around it are deliberately empty days: the Radika river, a monastery with the most extravagant carved iconostasis in the Balkans, and an afternoon spent watching a plateau do nothing. It suits people who like wood smoke, cash economies and the knowledge that the last confirmed stronghold of the Balkan lynx is in the forest below them.

trips.title: Połoniny and Dark Skies: Seven Off-Grid Days in the Bieszczady
trips.sub: The Bieszczady & the San Valley, Podkarpackie
trips.summary: Poland's far south-eastern corner is a landscape emptied by history. You sleep in wooden cabins with a stove you feed yourself, climb onto the połoniny, bare grass ridges running above the beech forest like a spine…

trips.title: Granite, Granaries and Wolf Country: Peneda-Gerês Slow Week
trips.summary: Peneda-Gerês is Portugal's only national park and it is not wilderness in the North American sense, it is a 700 km² granite massif that people have farmed, grazed and terraced for two thousand years, and the interest lies in that overlap. Espigueiros, the stone maize granaries at Soajo and Lindoso, stand on bare rock like a village of tombs. Garrano ponies graze commons that have been communal since medieval charters. Iberian wolf still runs the northern serras. This week moves anticlockwise from Soajo through Castro Laboreiro's high seasonal villages to Pitões das Júnias, then into the Gerês valley for the Roman road, the drowned village of Vilarinho das Furnas and the river pools. It suits people who like walking on granite, sleeping under a wooden ceiling, and eating slowly.

trips.title: Karst and Wooden Spires: Apuseni and Maramureș from a Cabin
trips.sub: Apuseni Nature Park (Bihor/Alba) and Maramureș (Iza, Vaser and the Rodna foothills)
trips.summary: Two Romanias that the country's own tourists barely reach. First a limestone plateau riddled with ice caves and swallow-holes, where the road ends in mud and the villages are single farmsteads scattered across whole…

trips.title: Ladders in the Waterfall: A Cabin Week in Slovenský raj and on Muránska planina
trips.sub: Slovenský raj National Park and Muránska planina
trips.summary: There is nowhere else in Europe where the official trail goes straight up the inside of a waterfall on bolted iron ladders, one way only, with the water hitting your boots. Slovenský raj is a small national park of…

trips.title: Dehesa, Vultures and Dark Sky: An Extremadura Slow Week
trips.sub: Monfragüe, Las Hurdes, Sierra de Gata & the Jerte
trips.summary: Extremadura is Europe's largest surviving stretch of dehesa, open oak pasture grazed for a thousand years, and its wildlife density is a consequence of that farming, not despite it. This week is built around slowness: two long, low-mileage days at Monfragüe's cliff viewpoints where cinereous vultures pass at eye level, a day of schist villages in Las Hurdes where the roofs are slate and the valleys are hard, a gorge day in the Jerte, and evenings under one of the darkest certified skies in western Europe. It suits people with binoculars, patience, and no urge to tick off towns. The best raptor watching is in the first two hours of light and the last two before dusk, so this is a trip that wants early nights and earlier mornings.

trips.title: Stay on the Path: A Week in the Swiss National Park
trips.summary: A week inside the strictest nature reserve in the Alps: marked paths only, nothing picked, no camping and no dogs, from Zernez to a hut with no road and Val Trupchun's ibex and red deer.
